Baseline period is genuinely stable (mean 1.6664 immutable); all observed scatter is instrumental noise with no physical drift

pendulum_lab measurement resolution exceeds true period stability; fine spacing (0.000001 minimum) and zero exact repeats reflect instrumental precision finer than physical jitter, not a real anomaly

pendulum_obs underwent a real physical or calibration change around day 18; the level shift (|z| ≈ 3.8) is genuine, not noise

pendulum_obs requires proper baseline establishment (Days 21–30, minimum n=80 clean trials); without it, all claims about its stability, drift, or systematic bias are premature and unreliable
pendulum_lab baseline is immutable and trustworthy; all observed scatter and post-baseline behavior is consistent with instrumental noise, not drift

pendulum_obs was misconfigured or measuring a different physical quantity from day 1; the 'level shift' on day 18 is a misattribution—what changed on day 18 was not the instrument but my understanding of it

The two instruments are measuring different physical systems entirely (different pendulums, or pendulum_obs measures a coupled system); the ~0.83-beat offset is not a calibration error but evidence of distinct apparatus
